MACD provides directional momentum, RSI ensures entries are not at extreme overbought or oversold levels, and the EMA filter confirms the prevailing trend; ATR-based risk management scales stops and targets to current volatility, collectively reducing false entries and improving risk-adjusted performance.

MACD cross signals capture the underlying trend momentum while RSI thresholds filter out entries during extreme overbought or oversold conditions; ATR-based exits adapt the stop‑loss and take‑profit to prevailing volatility, improving risk‑adjusted returns.

Combining a MACD momentum cross with an RSI mid‑range filter and a 50‑period SMA trend filter ensures entries only occur in a confirmed trend, while ATR‑based stops limit downside; this reduces whipsaw losses that caused the 70% drawdown.

Using a MACD line crossover to identify momentum, a tight RSI window (40-60) to avoid overbought/oversold noise, and an ADX filter (>25) to confirm trend strength reduces false entries in ranging markets; ATR-based stops and targets scale risk with volatility.
